title: Named volumes
idea: A named volume is storage that Docker creates and manages by name. Its data survives when the container that used it is removed.
points: `docker run -v covers:/app/covers` mounts the volume `covers`, creating it if needed.
`docker rm` removes the container but keeps its named volumes.
Docker decides where the data lives; you refer to it by name.
A new, empty volume is filled with the image's files from the mount path.

steps.caption: `docker run -v covers:/app/covers` creates the volume `covers` and starts the first container with it mounted.
Say the app saves two cover images. They are written to the volume, not the container's own writable layer.
`docker rm -f api` deletes the container and its writable layer. The volume and its files stay.
A new container started with the same `-v` mounts the volume and sees the same files.
Remove the containers, then run `docker volume rm covers`. The volume and its files are gone for good.

code.caption: Imagine the API saves cover images in `/app/covers`. Remove its container, reuse the volume, and the files remain.

walk.text: Create the volume up front. Optional: `docker run` creates a missing volume.
Mount it at `/app/covers`. Files the app writes there go into the volume.
Force-remove the container. The volume is not touched.
Start a new `api` with the same `-v`. It sees the earlier files.
List the volumes on this Docker host.
Show the details of one volume.

pitfalls: `docker volume rm` deletes the data for good; back up anything you still need.
Always name the volume: `-v /app/covers` creates an anonymous volume with a random name.
Reusing a volume that already has data hides the image's files at that path.

quiz.q: You run `docker rm -f api`. What happens to the named volume `covers` it used?
options: It is deleted with the container
It stays, but its files are emptied
It stays, with all its files
Docker asks whether to keep it
quiz.why: Named volumes are managed apart from containers. Removing a container leaves the volume and its files in place.

takeaway: Named volumes outlive containers; mount the same one to keep your data.
